title: EmailAddress.name / AddressGroup.name trim-and-None-on-empty behavior undocumented
description:
header_typed.rs:42-43 EmailAddress.name doc: "Display name from the `mailbox`, RFC 2047 encoded-words already decoded."

header_typed.rs:57-58 AddressGroup.name doc: "Display name of the group, or `None` for ungrouped mailboxes."

Implementation (convert_addr lines 281-302 and group_addresses lines 321-348) performs additional transformations that the doc does not mention:

1. Surrounding ASCII whitespace is trimmed off the decoded display name.
2. A name that is empty after trimming is mapped to `None` rather than to `Some(String::new())`.

These are intentional per the RFC 8621 §4.1.2.3 quoting rules cited in the source comment, but the public-facing doc on the EmailAddress / AddressGroup struct fields does not state them. RFC 8621 is not part of mime-tree's caller contract — callers depending on this crate do not have to read RFC 8621 to know what the fields contain.

Caller-facing consequence: a caller round-tripping a header (parse, edit, serialize) will silently lose leading/trailing whitespace in display names. A caller checking `email.name.is_some()` to detect "name was present in source" gets a false negative when the name was `"   "` (whitespace only). Without doc, this is a bug-shaped surprise.

Fix: update the EmailAddress.name and AddressGroup.name doc comments to state the trim + empty-becomes-None behavior, citing RFC 8621 §4.1.2.3 if useful.
close_reason: Documentation batch on the typed header surface: (.7) parse_header_typed now states trailing CRLF is permitted-but-not-required (matching the implementation); (.8) EmailAddress.name and AddressGroup.name field docs now state the trim+empty-to-None normalization; (.12) HeaderValueTyped doc has a Serde Wire Format section pinning the current externally-tagged shape and explicitly distinguishing it from RFC 8621 wire format (callers responsible for that mapping); (.17) parse_header_typed doc now carries one runnable example per HeaderForm variant (six total); (.24) HeaderDateTime has an Equality Semantics section noting derived PartialEq is field-wise not instant-wise, with a worked example and the to_timestamp escape hatch; (.25) EmailAddress has an Equality Semantics section noting derived PartialEq is byte-exact (no RFC 5321 domain case-folding) and pointing callers at manual canonicalisation; (.30) parse_header_typed doc has an Empty-Result Ambiguity table making explicit that callers cannot distinguish malformed-vs-empty-vs-non-UTF-8 and flagging the future-direction (strict variant / warnings tuple). No code changes.
